topic.title: Vision-Language Agents for Grounded Planning
topic.overview: Grounded agents must connect visual observations and language instructions to executable actions. The representatives cover navigation, robotic manipulation, latent planning, and evaluation of embodied decision-making. They distinguish understanding a scene or instruction from tracking progress and acting successfully over a sequence of changing observations.
topic.whyItMatters: Strong answers to visual questions do not automatically translate into reliable control. Benchmarks that test low-level actions, temporal understanding, and interacting constraints reveal gaps hidden by high-level language competence.
topic.evolution: The collection begins with language-perception grounding and compositional robot tasks, then includes demonstration-based synthesis. The 2023–2025 representatives emphasize multimodal foundation agents and comprehensive navigation or manipulation evaluation. Recent work broadens planning tests to realistic interfaces and tightly coupled constraints, while new vision-language-action recipes target the bridge from perception to control.
openQuestions: How can agents detect that their understanding no longer matches execution progress?
Which evaluations distinguish visual comprehension from robust long-horizon control?

papers.title: Real-Time Execution of Action Chunking Flow Policies

papers.title: SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models

papers.title: Semantic Glitch: Agency and Artistry in an Autonomous Pixel Cloud

papers.title: SimWorld-Robotics: Synthesizing Photorealistic and Dynamic Urban Environments for Multimodal Robot Navigation and Collaboration

papers.title: Towards Reliable Code-as-Policies: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Embodied Task Planning

papers.title: VLA-Cache: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation via Adaptive Token Caching

papers.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning

papers.title: Code2Worlds: Empowering Coding LLMs for 4D World Generation
